speaker: Pieter van der Meer
description: This talk explores Voyager’s 1970s-era communication coding, the Viterbi algorithm, and modern machine-learning approaches to decoding deep-space signals. It compares vintage engineering ingenuity with today’s tools through real examples and demonstrations, showing how classic algorithms and AI c...

title: Bootiful Security
speaker: Daniel Garnier-Moiroux
description: Passkeys offer a passwordless future with stronger, simpler authentication. This talk by Daniel Garnier Moiroux and Josh Long explores how Spring Security 7 can help replace passwords, improve security, and streamline login experiences for users and systems.

title: Their API Went Down. So Why Is My App on Fire?
speaker: Ines Panker
description: The talk explains how to protect your app from outages in APIs you don’t control. Beyond try-except, it covers practical patterns like caching 429s, resuming syncs, and using circuit breakers to prevent external failures from cascading into your own production system.

title: Production-Ready Java Containers: Smaller, Faster, Smarter
speaker: Albert Attard
description: This session explores optimizing Java containers using tailored runtimes with jlink, CDS, AOT, JVM container awareness, memory tuning, and efficient image-building practices. Through progressive measurement, it examines trade-offs among size, startup, warmup, memory, throughput, observability, se...

title: What Does it Print? The Java Quiz (Hard Edition 🤯)
speaker: Clément de Tastes
description: Interactive Java session exploring tricky language subtleties through short code snippets. Participants will predict outputs together, revisit core concepts, challenge assumptions, and deepen their understanding of how Java actually behaves in practice.

title: Open Source in the Age of AI: Where's the value?
speaker: Trisha Gee
description: This talk explores how AI changes the value of open source, asking whether libraries and tools remain commercially useful when AI can generate code. It brings together maintainers and contributors to discuss funding, community, business models, and the purpose of open source in an AI-driven world.

title: F*ck The System, and other bad ideas for the future
speaker: Jo Caudron
description: A provocative manifesto exploring today’s geopolitical upheaval and asking how Europe can become sovereign, resilient, and innovative in the emerging world order. title: The Praxis proxy or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love AI workloads
speaker: Alex Snaps
description: Praxis is an open-source Rust proxy framework built for AI traffic, enabling body-based routing, credential isolation, streaming, token-cost controls, and MCP support. Unlike traditional proxies, it uses composable filters for routing, guardrails, rate limiting, and custom logic, letting teams bu...

title: Escaping Java's Allocation Gravity with Value Classes
speaker: Clément de Tastes
description: This talk introduces Java’s Project Valhalla value types through a black hole simulation, showing how they improve immutability, memory efficiency, and performance for heavy numerical workloads. It also explores experimental non-nullable `!` syntax, optimization potential, current limitations, an...

title: Why it takes 3000 commits to bring Valhalla's value objects to the JDK
speaker: David Simms
description: JEP 401 Value Objects arrives in OpenJDK preview, enabling a new Java type model with minimal code changes. The talk explains what value objects are, JVM benefits, Valhalla history, implementation details, and the path toward bridging objects and primitives, including future support like `List`.

title: All you need to know about Maven 4!
speaker: Matthias Bünger
description: This talk explores Maven 4’s long-awaited development, the challenges of evolving a mature ecosystem without breaking compatibility, and the motivations behind its redesign. It also highlights key new features and improvements in the upcoming major release.

title: The Quantum Tech Lead: Hands-On and Abstract at the Same Time
speaker: Cristian Schuszter
description: This talk explores the transition from individual contributor to technical leader, showing how leadership can amplify impact rather than reduce it. Drawing on experience at CERN, it shares practical techniques for adapting, staying relevant, and maintaining technical influence while leading teams.

title: Embabel Agent v1.5
speaker: Rod Johnson
description: Embabel is a JVM-native agent framework built on Spring AI and Spring Boot that replaces LLM-driven decision-making with deterministic Goal-Oriented Action Planning (GOAP). title: Is AI killing XP practices? (Or are we letting it?)
speaker: Nacho Cougil
description: AI can tempt teams to skip core XP practices like TDD, refactoring, pair programming, and CI. This session shows why these habits are at risk in AI-assisted development, what breaks when they’re ignored, and why they matter even more as AI accelerates both good and bad engineering.

title: What’s happening with Project Amber?
speaker: Gavin Bierman
description: Project Amber is advancing Java’s data-oriented programming with new pattern-matching features: user-defined deconstruction, nested constant patterns, exhaustive matching, safer primitive conversions, and compact record reconstruction. title: You thought technical debt was bad? Meet design debt!
speaker: Julien Topçu
description: The talk argues that technical debt is only the surface of deeper accidental design debt, which can worsen despite best practices like refactoring, KISS, and YAGNI. It explores how design debt forms, affects architecture and business, and how to detect, assess, and prevent it.

title: 10 Billion Records vs. The Regulator: An Architectural Post-Mortem of an 11TB Exadata Failure
speaker: Martin Ladecky
description: A major bank incident triggered a BaFin investigation after an 11TB Oracle Exadata system failed at 10 billion records. title: Java Next - From Valhalla to Leyden, from Babylon to Panama, from Amber to Detroit
speaker: Nicolai Parlog
description: This talk explores Java’s evolution and future through major projects: Valhalla’s unified type system, Leyden’s faster startup, Babylon’s foreign models and hardware support, Panama’s native interoperability, Amber’s expressive language features, Loom’s structured concurrency, and Detroit’s Pytho...

title: Strangling the dragon: modernizing legacy systems with the Strangler Fig pattern
speaker: Daniel Raneland
description: The talk argues against full rewrites of legacy systems, citing risk and the second system effect. It promotes the Strangler Fig pattern for gradual replacement, combined with Domain-Driven Design and the Inverse Conway Manoeuvre to align system architecture with team structure.

title: My old trains have a second life, with TinyGo!
speaker: Florian FORESTIER
description: A retro model train hobby project was modernized with Seeed Studio hardware, Bluetooth, and TinyGo to create a digital railway network with individual train control for speed, direction, and lights. The talk covers embedded hardware/software architecture, lessons learned, and open-source implemen...

title: We created our own AI orchestrator and it became so much more!
speaker: Ricky van Rijn
description: We built an agent orchestration tool using Embabel Agent, Skills, and Spec files to coordinate AI-driven software work. It provides a visual dashboard for active agents, tasks, and next steps, reshaping team roles: developers review AI output, analysts define requirements, and product owners mana...

title: 10 boring reasons why Java is the best ecosystem for agentic development
speaker: Ed Burns
description: The talk argues that Java’s “boring” strengths—types, tests, static analysis, mature builds, formatting, observability, and more—help control AI agents’ risks like hallucinations, non-determinism, and unmaintainable code.
